lessons.title: Evictable large-value cache
lessons.objective: Cache and retrieve one bounded blob while keeping provider availability, authority, retention, integrity, and eviction outcomes explicit.
lessons.prose: Cache nodes cross an ordinary bounded host-service boundary. Put returns an opaque provider- and run-scoped handle; get verifies the content digest before yielding bytes; remove invalidates one handle. The installed provider is best effort and evictable, never durable, and a handle never substitutes for a grant.
lessons.source:
panel 0

node blob : storage/blob/literal {
    value = bytes("626f756e64656420636163686520666978747572650a")
    maximum_bytes = 64
}

node put : storage/cache/put {
    resource = secret("conduit.resource/storage-cache-example-put")
    grant = secret("conduit.grant/storage-cache-put")
    descriptor = ref("conduit.descriptor/storage-cache-example")
    run_epoch = 1
    now_tick = 10
    retention_ticks = 100
    maximum_blob_bytes = 64
    persistence = "evictable"
    eviction = "fifo"
    sensitivity = "restricted"
    cancellation = "discard"
}

node get : storage/cache/get {
    resource = secret("conduit.resource/storage-cache-example-get")
    grant = secret("conduit.grant/storage-cache-get")
    descriptor = ref("conduit.descriptor/storage-cache-example")
    run_epoch = 1
    now_tick = 11
    maximum_blob_bytes = 64
    integrity = "sha256-before-yield"
    cancellation = "discard"
}

cord blob.blob -> put.blob { capacity = 1 max_value_bytes = 64 max_queued_bytes = 64 low_watermark = 0 high_watermark = 1 pressure = block }
cord put.handle -> get.handle { capacity = 1 max_value_bytes = 66 max_queued_bytes = 66 low_watermark = 0 high_watermark = 1 pressure = block }
hints: The handle is an opaque reference scoped to this provider and run; get still needs its own active grant.
Best effort describes the provider class, while a fresh host observation describes current selectability. Neither promises future uptime.
A hit validates SHA-256 identity before bytes cross the output cord; miss, eviction, expiration, provider loss, and cancellation remain distinct outcomes.
lessons.solution: Wire an explicitly bounded blob into put, pass only its opaque handle to get or remove, pin a fresh provider report and separate operation grants in the exact plan, and request evictable retention only.

accessibility.non_audio: An ordered text table names provider observation freshness, best-effort class, resource and grant, blob digest and byte count, opaque handle scope, queue pressure, retention, hit or miss, cancellation, error, and terminal cause.
accessibility.keyboard: Native controls plus Space to play and ArrowRight to step while the ordered cache story has focus.
accessibility.color_independent: Every state is duplicated by provider, handle, digest, bound, hit, miss, evicted, expired, cancelled, error, and terminal text.

library.summary: Explicit typed cache nodes store bounded blobs through an optional best-effort provider without claiming durability.
library.what: Blob literal produces bounded bytes; put stores them and returns an opaque handle; get checks identity before a hit; remove invalidates the referenced entry.
library.when: Use this profile when recomputable large values may be retained locally for reuse and a miss or provider loss can be handled explicitly.
library.wrong: Durable requirements, stale reports, insufficient capacity, oversized values, denied grants, refused sensitivity, digest mismatch, wrong provider or run handles, cancellation, eviction, expiration, and provider loss fail or report explicit outcomes with no hidden fallback.
library.provider: explicit browser in-memory evictable cache provider through the ordinary exact host-service boundary
expected_evidence: known contract, installed provider, fresh host observation, best-effort availability class, active operation grant, and resource binding
exact implementation, artifact, descriptor, provider epoch, run epoch, handle slot and generation, content digest and byte count
finite entry, byte, retention, pending-operation, queue, timer, cancellation, and evidence bounds
ordered put then integrity-checked hit, or explicit miss, eviction, expiration, remove, provider loss, cancellation, error, and terminal cause
protected resource and grant configuration remains redacted

scenarios.title: Put then integrity-checked get
scenarios.explanation: Store one bounded blob, pass the opaque handle across a bounded cord, and verify its content identity before yielding a hit.

scenarios.title: Put then explicit remove
scenarios.explanation: Invalidate one opaque handle under a separate remove grant; the handle itself never authorizes removal.

scenarios.title: Durability is not cacheability
scenarios.explanation: Changing the requirement to durable is rejected deterministically; an evictable provider is never relabeled or ranked into durable storage.

scenarios.title: Wrong resource or grant
scenarios.explanation: A handle cannot repair a missing resource binding or mint authority; admission fails before cache mutation.

scenarios.title: Cancelled before first operation
scenarios.explanation: Cancellation discards the pending cache operation and yields no handle, cached value, or hidden background work.

lessons.title: Fan-out is a choice
lessons.objective: Choose an explicit bounded fan-out contract when one value must reach more than one sink.
lessons.prose: The tee contract makes duplication and branch pressure explicit. Its receiving value port and outgoing left and right ports are visible in source, and each sink receives one value.
lessons.source:
panel 0

node greeting : std/literal {
    value = "Fan out.\n"
}
node messages : std/text/lines {
    maximum_line_bytes = 1024
    maximum_retained_prefix_bytes = 1024
}
node split : conduit.std/tee {
    mode = "coupled"
}
node left_text : std/text/join {
    separator = ""
    maximum_items = 8
    maximum_item_bytes = 1024
    maximum_separator_bytes = 64
    maximum_output_bytes = 4096
}
node right_text : std/text/join {
    separator = ""
    maximum_items = 8
    maximum_item_bytes = 1024
    maximum_separator_bytes = 64
    maximum_output_bytes = 4096
}
node first : display/text
node second : display/text

cord greeting.value -> messages.text {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 1024
    max_queued_bytes = 1024
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
cord messages.line -> split.value {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 1024
    max_queued_bytes = 1024
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
cord split.left -> left_text.item {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 1024
    max_queued_bytes = 1024
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
cord split.right -> right_text.item {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 1024
    max_queued_bytes = 1024
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
cord left_text.text -> first.text {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 4096
    max_queued_bytes = 4096
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
cord right_text.text -> second.text {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 4096
    max_queued_bytes = 4096
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
hints: The tee's coupled mode admits one value only when both outgoing branches can accept it.
Each cord declares its own finite capacity and pressure rule.
lessons.solution: Split the finite text batch into line values, tee messages.line into two explicit branches, join each finite branch, then connect both joined text values to distinct display ports.

accessibility.non_audio: Both delivered values appear as text output.

lessons.title: Typed text formatting
lessons.objective: Format bounded text, split logical lines, and join a finite item stream while inspecting the exact graph and ordered evidence story.
lessons.prose: The formatter emits one typed text value. Lines removes LF or CRLF delimiters without depending on implementation chunks; join retains a finite bounded item stream and emits one ordered result.
hints: The template and values inputs have different exact value types.
Select a scenario, edit its typed node configuration, and rerun.
Timeline controls reveal existing evidence; they do not execute the graph.
lessons.solution: Connect std/text and std/format-values producers to the formatter's exact inputs, then connect its std/text output to a consumer.

accessibility.non_audio: Every graph event is also an ordered table row with sequence, tick, subject, event, pressure, occupancy, and terminal cause.
accessibility.keyboard: Native controls plus Space to play and ArrowRight to step while the execution story has focus.
accessibility.color_independent: Event labels, lane names, marker shapes, table text, and graph selection duplicate every color cue.

library.summary: Bounded format, lines, and join nodes turn typed text into exact finite graph operations.
library.what: Format substitutes typed values; lines emits delimiter-free LF/CRLF logical lines; join inserts one separator between a finite ordered item set.
library.when: Use them when panel data must become bounded text, line-oriented values, or one finite combined value without provider-specific conventions.
library.wrong: Malformed placeholders, invalid UTF-8, oversized lines or items, an open-ended join input, and retained or output overflow terminate with exact codes.
expected_evidence: node preparation and value derivation
ordered cord acceptance and consumption
block pressure policy and occupancy
one exact terminal cause

lessons.title: Bounded flow control
lessons.objective: Run the canonical tee, merge, zip, gate, and select contracts and inspect the exact ordering, pressure, retained-state, and terminal facts that make their behavior portable.
lessons.prose: These nodes shape a stream without inventing a universal value type. This lesson uses their exact std/text instantiations, capacity-one block pressure, finite retained state, and explicit terminal policies.
hints: Select one standalone scenario before changing its supported configuration.
Capacity and pressure belong to each cord; ordering and retained-state policy belong to the selected node contract.
The timeline is a projection of bounded evidence and never changes the resolved plan.
lessons.solution: Use the canonical conduit.std identities, exact typed ports, supported finite configuration, and capacity-one blocking cords; inspect the resolved plan before treating the timeline as evidence.

accessibility.non_audio: An ordered text table names sequence, node, port, pressure result, occupancy, retained-value count, ordering decision, terminal input, and final cause.
accessibility.keyboard: Native controls plus Space to play and ArrowRight to step while the ordered flow story has focus.
accessibility.color_independent: Port labels, branch numbers, ordering ordinals, terminal words, and table text duplicate every graph color.

library.summary: Five canonical structural nodes provide bounded fan-out, merge, pairing, admission, and selection.
library.what: Tee duplicates one value to two branches; merge chooses available inputs round-robin; zip emits complete pairs; gate admits data only while open; select consumes only its active input.
library.when: Use these nodes when stream topology needs an explicit, inspectable structural policy instead of hidden callback or host-channel behavior.
library.wrong: Legacy flow/* identities, duplicate port IDs, wake-order races, partial coupled publication, unbounded retention, implicit dropping, and fabricated terminal success fail closed.
expected_evidence: exact contract, implementation, artifact, and port bindings
capacity-one block pressure and queue occupancy
round-robin input ordinal or control-priority decision
bounded retained-value usage and one exact terminal cause

scenarios.title: Coupled tee
scenarios.semantics: Both branches reserve in one scheduler transaction; block pressure rolls the whole step back.

scenarios.title: Round-robin merge
scenarios.semantics: One available value is chosen per input ordinal cycle; completion drains both inputs.

scenarios.title: Pairwise zip
scenarios.semantics: At most one value per side is retained; both outputs publish in one scheduler transaction.

scenarios.title: Controlled gate
scenarios.semantics: Control is processed before data; closed block mode retains values only in bounded input queues.

scenarios.title: Controlled select
scenarios.semantics: Control is processed before the selected input; inactive block mode leaves the other queue untouched.

scenarios.title: Select then tee
scenarios.semantics: The selected exact text value reaches both coupled branches with the same handle and terminal cause.

lessons.title: Bounded in-run state
lessons.objective: Run a cell, duplicate suppressor, and in-run cache while inspecting their exact state schema, bounds, deterministic eviction, restart, and terminal facts.
lessons.prose: State is local to one exact run and has a declared shape and ceiling. A cell keeps one current value, deduplicate retains collision-safe identities, and cache retains a finite key/value table; none implies persistence or external storage.
hints: State bounds and restart policy belong to the node contract, while queue pressure remains on each cord.
Deduplicate uses exact byte equality identities and FIFO count/byte eviction; duplicate drop is explicit.
The cache is in-run only: TTL and checkpoints are unsupported and restart empties it.
lessons.solution: Pin the state or request schema and equality descriptor, choose finite entry and byte ceilings, and declare eviction, reset, restart, checkpoint, sensitivity, and terminal behavior.

accessibility.non_audio: An ordered table names each value, state generation, retained count and bytes, duplicate decision, cache hit or miss, eviction, and terminal cause.
accessibility.keyboard: Native controls plus Space to play and ArrowRight to step through exact state transitions.
accessibility.color_independent: Value labels, generation numbers, hit/miss words, eviction ordinals, and terminal text duplicate every graph color.

library.summary: Three exact providers expose one-value register state, duplicate suppression, and a bounded in-run cache.
library.what: Cell emits its configured initial and updated values; deduplicate admits only identities outside its finite FIFO window; cache executes explicit put, get, invalidate, and reset requests.
library.when: Use them when state changes graph-visible behavior within a run and must remain bounded, deterministic, inspectable, and disposable at restart.
library.wrong: Unpinned equality, hidden persistence, ambient TTL, automatic checkpointing, unbounded entries or bytes, collision-unsafe comparison, and cross-run retention fail closed.

contracts.policy: initial or empty; reset=initial; restart=initial; checkpoint=unsupported
sha256 byte equality; FIFO count/byte window; duplicate=drop; restart=empty

library.provider: hosted exact-plan deterministic executor with in-run caller-bounded state
expected_evidence: exact state/equality/request schema and provider bindings
retained entry and byte high-water facts
duplicate, hit, miss, update, invalidate, reset, and FIFO eviction decisions
restart/checkpoint policy and one exact terminal cause

scenarios.title: Cell updates

lessons.prose: Process execution is one optional host boundary, not a shell and not a substitute for a semantic node.     working_resource = secret("conduit.resource/process-working-root")
    grant = secret("conduit.grant/process-exec")
    stdin_close = "close-after-input"
    maximum_stdin_bytes = 4096
    maximum_stdout_bytes = 4096
    maximum_stderr_bytes = 4096
    maximum_chunk_bytes = 1024
    maximum_pending_operations = 3
    maximum_processes = 1
    maximum_child_processes = 0

    maximum_environment_bytes = 16
    maximum_work = 4096
    maximum_evidence_events = 64
    deadline_ticks = 1000
    graceful_signal = 9
    graceful_ticks = 1
    forced_ticks = 1

}
